changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.29[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]Fixed: Kodi closing on its own[/COLOR]
-Kodi could quit when you came back to the Home after playing something. The skin reloads the luc_kodi rows when playback starts and stops, and Kodi's "reuse language invoker" can crash at that moment (Kodi issue #27025). It is now off for everyone; Developer mode can still turn it on.
-FENtastic and FENtastic Plus: the ratings on the Home could be written to a skin window that Kodi had already rebuilt, which can close Kodi. luc_kodi no longer keeps that window.
-Home rows that cannot be refreshed (no network, TMDb or Trakt not answering) now wait 15 minutes before trying again. Before, Nimbus Plus reloaded every row each minute while the network was down.
[COLOR fffdb515]Faster and lighter source search[/COLOR]
-While sources come in, luc_kodi only looks at the new ones instead of the whole list each time. With 1,000 sources each check went from about 1.5 ms to under 0.01 ms, and it runs forty times a second.
-The search window is redrawn only when something on it changes, about three quarters fewer calls to Kodi during a search.
-The background of the source list loads in the background, so the list opens without a stutter.
-What the search finds, when it stops and what it shows are the same as before.
[COLOR fffdb515]AI Search[/COLOR]
-While Gemini works, a window shows your request, the model being tried and the seconds, with a Cancel button.
-Cancel stops at once and takes you back to the AI Search list. Searches already saved open straight away.
-One search never takes more than 45 seconds; before, it could run to about 70.
[COLOR fffdb515]Cleanup[/COLOR]
-Saved source lists older than a week are now removed. Before, the lists of titles you never opened again stayed forever, and they are the largest part of the providers database.
-The search speed database sets itself up once per session and clears old entries at most every ten minutes.
-Automatic trailers on the Nimbus Home no longer leave an error in the log.
